evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: Not asked. Rep jumps directly into pricing discussion without probing concerns.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no concerns were raised by customer.
evidence_quotes.value_days: Rep offered Wed/Thurs packing/moving dates but customer requested Tues/Thurs instead. Rep accommodated but never mentioned cost savings or anchored value; no flexibility ask about cheaper days.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: Rate lock mentioned: 'this quote is available to you for as long as you needed to. We, it doesn't have any expiration' and 'we do not require any deposit or do we have any rescheduling fees.' But no explicit ask for the business — rep says 'I'm gonna send you an email with everything we talked about today' and customer says she'll call back, ending with customer saying 'I'll call back tomorrow.'

top_strength: Jules delivered clear, comprehensive pricing transparency upfront—hourly rate, what's included, truck fee, packing materials, 2.5-hour minimum, and 15-minute prorating—without hiding fees.
coaching_note: Before pricing, always ask the two-concerns question ('movers showing up on time or damage to items') and probe two layers deep on what matters to the customer, then deliver the two promises—this shapes everything that follows and is the foundation of the whole call.
